results.title: 15 GPU list prices rose in September and none fell. Today AWS raises Capacity Blocks 15% - DEV Community
results.author: FastGPU
highlights:
# 15 GPU list prices rose in September and none fell. Today AWS raises Capacity Blocks 15% 

In September 2026 we compared 176 posted on-demand GPU prices, each cloud's own published rate for each GPU it rents, between the first three and the last three days of the month. 15 ended the month higher, none ended it lower, and the other 161 did not move.

Today, October 7, AWS adds an increase of its own to EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML.

Everything below comes from the daily prices FastGPU records across GPU clouds, published as an open dataset, and from AWS's own pricing page. Every figure links to the page it comes from.

## 15 increases, no cuts 

All 15 came from two providers: Verda (10) and RunPod (5). Marketplaces, where each host sets its own price, are not part of this count.

| Provider | GPU | Sep 1 to 3 | Sep 28 to 30 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Verda | H200 | $4.00 | $4.64 | +16.0% |
| RunPod | A100 80GB | $1.39 | $1.59 | +14.4% |
| Verda | GB300 | $8.62 | $9.72 | +12.8% |
| Verda | B300 | $7.50 | $8.45 | +12.7% |
| Verda | L40S | $1.37 | $1.54 | +12.4% |
| Verda | B200 | $6.11 | $6.85 | +12.1% |
| Verda | V100 | $0.17 | $0.19 | +11.8% |
| Verda | RTX 6000 Ada | $1.04 | $1.16 | +11.5% |
| RunPod | A40 | $0.44 | $0.49 | +11.4% |
| RunPod | RTX PRO 6000 | $1.89 | $2.09 | +10.6% |
| RunPod | L40S | $0.99 | $1.09 | +10.1% |
| Verda | H100 SXM | $3.25 | $3.56 | +9.5% |
| RunPod | H100 SXM | $3.29 | $3.49 | +6.1% |
| Verda | A6000 | $0.61 | $0.64 | +4.9% |
| Verda | RTX PRO 6000 | $1.89 | $1.96 | +3.7% |

## The typical price rose less 

The median of each provider's lowest posted on-demand price, counting only the providers that posted a price on all six of those days, so a provider joining or leaving never reads as a price move:

| GPU | Sep 1 to 3 | Sep 28 to 30 | Change | Providers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.55 | $3.70 | +4.3% | 16 |
| H200 | $4.14 | $4.38 | +5.7% | 14 |
| B200 | $6.18 | $6.25 | +1.1% | 12 |
| A100 80GB | $1.79 | $1.79 | -0.1% | 15 |

## The cheapest offer moves both ways 

The floor, the lowest posted on-demand price outside the hyperscalers (geometric mean of the first three days against the last three), is set by one or two providers at a time, so it swings:

- H100 SXM: $1.34 to $1.57 (+17.4%, set by 2 providers)
- H200: $2.60 to $2.16 (-17.1%, set by 2 providers)
- B200: $3.69 to $3.69 (0.0%, set by 1 provider)
- A100 80GB: $0.64 to $0.53 (-16.7%, set by 1 provider)

So the list prices at the larger GPU clouds drifted up while the cheapest deal stayed a moving target. For a job of a few hours, the floor is what you pay; for a quarter's budget, the list-price trend matters more.

...

## AWS Capacity Blocks: 15% more from today, up to 26.5% outside the US 

AWS's Capacity Blocks pricing page says:

> Effective October 7, 2026, hourly rates per accelerator across all available AWS Regions will be: P6-B300 at $16.146 ($16.819 in AWS GovCloud Regions), P6-B200 at $14.208 ($14.801 in AWS GovCloud Regions), P5en at $7.895, P5e at $6.866, P5 at $5.970, P4de at $2.546, and P4d at $1.696.

Against the rates AWS published before, as recorded in our price-change log, per GPU per hour:

| Instance | GPU | Before | From Oct 7 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | B300 | $14.040 | $16.146 | +15.0% |
| P6-B200 | B200 | $12.355 | $14.208 | +15.0% |
| P5en, US Regions | H200 | $6.865 | $7.895 | +15.0% |
| P5en, Europe and Asia Pacific | H200 | $6.241 | $7.895 | +26.5% |
| P5e | H200 | $5.970 | $6.866 | +15.0% |
| P5, US Regions | H100 SXM | $5.191 | $5.970 | +15.0% |
| P5, Europe, Asia Pacific and South America | H100 SXM | $4.720 | $5.970 | +26.5% |
| P4de | A100 80GB | $2.214 | $2.546 | +15.0% |
| P4d | A100 40GB | $1.475 | $1.696 | +15.0% |

AWS now charges one rate in every Region, so blocks that used to be cheaper outside the US (P5 and P5en) rise the most. AWS publishes these rates to a tenth of a cent; our log shows them rounded to the cent. AWS also says Capacity Block reservation prices are dynamic and are updated periodically based on supply and demand, and: "All other EC2 Capacity Block prices, as well as prices on fixed pricing models like On-Demand and Savings Plans, remain unchanged."

...

## Data and method 

Posted prices, not transactions. The September report is computed from the recorded daily prices once the month is over and then frozen; every dated change is in the price-change log, also as JSON at `https://fastgpu.co/api/v1/price-changes`. The daily series is an open dataset (CC BY 4.0). Live prices in this post are as of 2026-10-07 01:46 UTC; the linked pages show the current ones. Some provider links on FastGPU are affiliate links; tables and every "cheapest" figure are ordered strictly by price.

highlights:
The NVIDIA B200 SXM posted a 3.1% week-over-week increase in median hourly rental rates, moving from $6.23 to $6.42, according to AIMC observations. That single-point move masks meaningful dispersion across individual marketplaces: the spread between the lowest and highest listed rates this week spans more than a dollar per GPU-hour, a gap that carries material implications for operators sourcing at scale. The analysis that follows breaks down where B200 SXM is currently priced across each tracked marketplace, how individual platforms have shifted relative to last week's baseline, and how wide that inter-marketplace spread has become. All figures reflect listed spot rates at time of observation and do not account for reservation discounts, commitment tiers, or negotiated enterprise terms.

results.author: 智机玄同 发布于 2026年10月9日 3 分钟阅读
highlights:
# Verda GPU Cloud 怎么选？原 DataCrunch 的 A100、H100、H200、B200 价格和 10 分钟计费

Verda（原 DataCrunch）提供 A100、H100、H200、B200、L40S、RTX PRO 6000 等 GPU。本文解释 On-Demand、Spot、10 分钟预付结算和存储费用。

智机玄同发布于 2026年10月9日 3 分钟阅读

资料核查日期： 2026年10月9日。价格、库存和服务商规则可能变化，请以官方页面为准。

文章目录

如果你以前搜过 DataCrunch，现在看到 Verda 不要以为是另一家公司。

Verda 就是原来的 DataCrunch 品牌。

它现在已经把产品扩展成 GPU Instances、Instant Clusters、Serverless Containers 和独立存储。

## 当前 On-Demand GPU

截至 2026-10-09，Verda `/pricing` 页面公开的单 GPU On-Demand 配置包括：

- A100 SXM4 40GB：$1.37 / 小时
- A100 SXM4 80GB：$1.89 / 小时
- H100 SXM5 80GB：$3.93 / 小时
- H200 SXM5 141GB：$5.12 / 小时
- B200 SXM6 180GB：$7.42 / 小时
- L40S 48GB：$1.62 / 小时
- RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB：$2.17 / 小时

这些是 On-Demand，不是旁边更低的 Spot 价格。

## 10 分钟计费到底是什么意思

Verda 文档当前说明 PAYG 采用：

预付 10 分钟增量。

如果你在这 10 分钟结束前终止实例，未使用的部分会在下一计费周期自动退回。

所以它既不是“必须整小时”，也不是像 GPUBank 那样完全按秒实时扣。

本站因此把这一项单独标记成“预付 10 分钟”。

results.title: Verda explained: GPU cloud, serverless and pricing
results.author: Sequenced desk
highlights:
Verda brings several ways of running AI workloads into one GPU cloud: individual instances, multi-node clusters and serverless containers. The company previously operated as DataCrunch. Its current offer is most useful when a team needs to move between experimentation, training and deployment without pretending those workloads have identical storage, latency or billing requirements.

...

Verda’s rebrand announcement describes the transition from DataCrunch to Verda as a change of name with the same company, team and platform. The announcement set the website transition for November 2025. Older DataCrunch references therefore belong to this company history rather than a separate competing provider.

...

## 04 / Pricing The same GPU name can carry a different service price

The public pricing page separates GPU instances from serverless configurations. The entries below are USD figures consulted on 23 September 2026. CPU, memory and deployment arrangements differ between services, so the H100 rows are not interchangeable quotations for an identical bundle.

| Service | Published rate or basis | Qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100 GPU instance | $3.38 per hour | On-demand instance configuration listed on the page. |
| H100 serverless container | $3.72 per hour | Separate serverless configuration; per-replica ten-minute billing intervals. |
| Instant Clusters | On-demand per GPU-hour; reserved arrangements by quote | Confirm node topology, term and available capacity. |
| Shared filesystem | $0.20 per GiB per month shown | Confirm metered units in the quote; do not infer a converted storage total. |

Published Verda pricing and serverless billing, consulted 23 September 2026. Capacity and configuration remain subject to the current offer.

results.title: On August 30 the cheapest published B200 rate across the nine providers we track, $6.69 per GPU-hour, sat $0.64 below the traded price. On September 21 it was still $6.69, and the … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
On August 30 the cheapest published B200 rate across the nine providers we track, $6.69 per GPU-hour, sat $0.64 below the traded price. On September 21 it was still $6.69, and the traded price was $1.02 above it.

That crossing is the issue. The Ornn Compute Price Index, a third-party index built from actual transactions, settled B200 at $7.71 per GPU-hour on September 21, the highest weekly reading we have recorded since we started tracking on May 18. It settled A100 at $0.99, the lowest. Over the same seven days not one comparable public on-demand rate across those nine providers moved more than 1%, and the four floors on our board have not moved since August 24.

...

A published rate is an asking price, not a promise of capacity. The Lambda listing behind that $6.69 names no region in this week's snapshot, so read it as a price rather than an offer. Leave it out and the market still sits $0.56 above the cheapest B200 rate across those nine that does name a region, Nebius at $7.15.

# B200 rates ran $3.69 to $16.11 a GPU-hour on October 3, 2026

The figure$3.69 Spread between B200 rate cards, on-demand · $3.69 (Deep Infra) to $16.11 (Google Cloud), 4.4× apart across 31 providers · read Oct 3, 05:40 UTC · source · live page

...

In the read of 05:40 UTC on October 3, 2026, the on-demand B200 rate cards on our pages ran from $3.69 per GPU-hour at Deep Infra to $16.11 at Google Cloud — 4.4× apart across 31 providers, with the median rate card at $6.79. Two of those 31 clouds entered the table the day before: Hostinger and Fireworks AI, both read for the first time on October 2, 2026. Hostinger’s B200 is the seventh lowest of the 31 at $4.50; Fireworks AI’s is the fourth highest at $13.00.

...

Fireworks AI’s table prints five cards: H100 80 GB GPU $8.00, H200 141 GB GPU $8.00, B200 180 GB GPU $13.00, B300 288 GB GPU $15.00 and GB300 288 GB GPU $20.00. The first two are the same figure for different memory. At this seller the 80 GB card and the 141 GB card carry one list price; across the rate cards we read on the same day they do not, the median H100 80GB rate card standing at $3.09 over 20 providers and the median H200 rate card at $4.38 over 42. Its GB300 figure is the dearest of the three rate cards that card has: $10.11 at Verda to $20.00 at Fireworks AI, 2.0× apart.

...

One thing these readings are not: a price change by either seller. October 2 is the day we first read these two pages, not a day either page was rewritten — we hold no earlier reading of them to compare against. Nothing here is forecast and nothing is a recommendation; every figure is a list price read at a stated time, and list prices are not availability.
